newsitem.title: USA: U.S. satisfied with Peru's handling of crisis.
newsitem.headline: U.S. satisfied with Peru's handling of crisis.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was satisfied with Peru's handling of the hostage crisis in Lima.

"I'm not going to second-guess what the Peruivian government's tactics are in dealing with the crisis...We are satisfied with the way the Peruvian government has dealt with the crisis thus far," John Dinger, a State Department spokesman, told reporters.

Although Dinger insisted the U.S. policy of not making concessions to terrorists remains unchanged, he refused to criticize Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori for indicating a willingness to consider letting Marxist rebels holding 83 hostages inside the Japanese ambassador's residencee seek asylum abroad.

"I understand that this is a position that President Fujimori has stated from the outset, that once the terrorists release all their hostages unharmned and lay down their arms he is willing to duscuss their demands," Dinger said.

"The United States position of course is well-known and unchanged. We do not make concessions to terrorists and we do not encourage others to," he said. But asked if allowing the rebels to seek safe haven was a concession, Dinger added: "I'm not going to put what President Fujimori says in the context of our position."
Peru's hostage crisis appeared to enter a tense endgame on Tuesday as Fujimori and top aides predicted a bloodless end to the two-week-old stand-off, but declined to rule out military action totally.
